entries.ex: Childhood *obesity* has risen sharply in many developed countries.
entries.exAr: ارتفعت معدلات *السمنة* لدى الأطفال ارتفاعًا حادًا في كثير من الدول المتقدمة.

entries.ex: Office workers who lead *sedentary* lives should take regular breaks to walk around.
entries.exAr: ينبغي للموظفين الذين يعيشون حياة *قليلة الحركة* أن يأخذوا فترات راحة منتظمة للمشي قليلًا.

entries.ex: A cholera *epidemic* can spread quickly in areas without clean drinking water.
entries.exAr: قد ينتشر *وباء* الكوليرا بسرعة في المناطق التي تفتقر إلى مياه الشرب النظيفة.

entries.ex: The COVID-19 *pandemic* forced millions of students to study from home.
entries.exAr: أجبرت *جائحة* كوفيد-19 ملايين الطلاب على الدراسة من المنزل.

entries.ex: Scientists developed a *vaccine* against the virus in less than a year.
entries.exAr: طوّر العلماء *لقاحًا* ضد الفيروس في أقل من عام.

entries.ex: Tiredness can be an early *symptom* of many serious illnesses.
entries.exAr: قد يكون التعب *عَرَضًا* مبكرًا لكثير من الأمراض الخطيرة.

entries.ex: Early *diagnosis* greatly improves the chances of surviving cancer.
entries.exAr: يزيد *التشخيص* المبكر فرص النجاة من السرطان زيادة كبيرة.

entries.ex: The new hospital offers free *treatment* for children under five.
entries.exAr: يقدّم المستشفى الجديد *علاجًا* مجانيًا للأطفال دون سن الخامسة.

entries.ex: Some strong painkillers can only be bought with a *prescription*.
entries.exAr: لا يمكن شراء بعض المسكنات القوية إلا *بوصفة طبية*.

entries.ex: Diabetes is a *chronic* condition that requires lifelong management.
entries.exAr: السكري حالة *مزمنة* تتطلب متابعة طوال الحياة.

entries.ex: Antibiotics can treat a bacterial *infection*, but they do not work against viruses.
entries.exAr: تعالج المضادات الحيوية *العدوى* البكتيرية، لكنها لا تؤثر في الفيروسات.

entries.ex: A balanced diet and enough sleep help to strengthen the *immune system*.
entries.exAr: يساعد النظام الغذائي المتوازن والنوم الكافي على تقوية *الجهاز المناعي*.

entries.ex: Employers are paying more attention to the *mental health* of their staff.
entries.exAr: يولي أصحاب العمل اهتمامًا متزايدًا *بالصحة النفسية* لموظفيهم.

entries.ex: Many students suffer from *anxiety* in the weeks before their final exams.
entries.exAr: يعاني كثير من الطلاب من *القلق* في الأسابيع التي تسبق امتحاناتهم النهائية.

entries.ex: Regular exercise has been shown to reduce the symptoms of *depression*.
entries.exAr: ثبت أن ممارسة الرياضة بانتظام تخفف أعراض *الاكتئاب*.

entries.ex: *Life expectancy* in Japan is among the highest in the world.
entries.exAr: يُعدّ *متوسط العمر المتوقع* في اليابان من بين الأعلى في العالم.

entries.ex: Many European countries provide free or low-cost *healthcare* to all citizens.
entries.exAr: توفّر كثير من الدول الأوروبية *رعاية صحية* مجانية أو منخفضة التكلفة لجميع المواطنين.

entries.ex: After the car accident, she needed *surgery* on her knee.
entries.exAr: بعد حادث السيارة، احتاجت إلى *عملية جراحية* في ركبتها.

entries.ex: Speech *therapy* can help children who have difficulty communicating.
entries.exAr: يمكن أن يساعد *علاج* النطق الأطفال الذين يجدون صعوبة في التواصل.

entries.ex: The patient made a full *recovery* after six weeks of rest.
entries.exAr: تعافى المريض *تعافيًا* تامًا بعد ستة أسابيع من الراحة.

entries.ex: Drowsiness is a common *side effect* of some allergy medicines.
entries.exAr: النعاس *أثر جانبي* شائع لبعض أدوية الحساسية.

entries.ex: Children with chickenpox should stay at home because the disease is highly *contagious*.
entries.exAr: ينبغي أن يبقى الأطفال المصابون بجدري الماء في المنزل لأن المرض *مُعدٍ* جدًا.

entries.ex: As the saying goes, *prevention* is better than cure.
entries.exAr: كما يقول المثل، *الوقاية* خير من العلاج.

entries.ex: Spending time in nature can improve our emotional *well-being*.
entries.exAr: يمكن أن يحسّن قضاء الوقت في الطبيعة *عافيتنا* النفسية.

entries.ex: Experts warn that *addiction* to online games is a growing problem among teenagers.
entries.exAr: يحذّر الخبراء من أن *إدمان* الألعاب الإلكترونية مشكلة متنامية بين المراهقين.

entries.ex: In remote villages, a single *physician* may be responsible for thousands of patients.
entries.exAr: في القرى النائية، قد يكون *طبيب* واحد مسؤولًا عن آلاف المرضى.

entries.ex: Good personal *hygiene*, such as washing your hands, helps to prevent the spread of disease.
entries.exAr: تساعد *النظافة* الشخصية الجيدة، مثل غسل اليدين، على منع انتشار الأمراض.

entries.ex: Poor *sanitation* is a major cause of disease in overcrowded cities.
entries.exAr: يُعدّ سوء *الصرف الصحي* سببًا رئيسيًا للأمراض في المدن المكتظة.

entries.ex: Elderly patients often take several types of *medication* every day.
entries.exAr: غالبًا ما يتناول المرضى المسنّون عدة أنواع من *الأدوية* يوميًا.

entries.ex: Public buildings should be fully accessible to people with a *disability*.
entries.exAr: ينبغي أن تكون المباني العامة متاحة بالكامل للأشخاص ذوي *الإعاقة*.

p1.q: What do you do to stay healthy?
p1.a: I try to walk for at least half an hour every day, because my job is quite *sedentary* and I spend most of the day at a desk. I also avoid sugary drinks and make sure I get enough sleep.

p1.q: How often do you go to the doctor?
p1.a: Not very often, thankfully. I usually go once a year for a general check-up, or if I have a *symptom* that doesn't go away, like a persistent cough. I believe *prevention* is always better than waiting until you're seriously ill.

p1.q: Do people in your country care about their health more than in the past?
p1.a: Yes, I'd say so. Twenty years ago few people went to the gym, but now fitness centres are everywhere. People are also more open about *mental health*, which used to be a taboo subject in my community.

p2.cue: Describe a time when you were ill or injured.
points: and explain how you felt during your recovery
p2.a: I'd like to describe a time about two years ago when I broke my ankle while playing football with friends. I slipped on wet grass, and I knew immediately that something was seriously wrong because the pain was unbearable. My brother drove me straight to the hospital, where a *physician* examined my foot and sent me for an X-ray. The *diagnosis* was a fractured ankle, and luckily I didn't need *surgery*. Instead, the doctors put my leg in a cast and gave me a *prescription* for painkillers, which made me a little sleepy, but that was the only *side effect*. My *recovery* took about three months. At first I felt frustrated, because I couldn't go to work or even climb the stairs easily. However, after several weeks of *therapy* with a physiotherapist, I slowly regained my strength. Looking back, the experience taught me to be more patient and to appreciate good health, which I had always taken for granted.

p3.q: Why do you think obesity is becoming more common?
p3.a: There are several reasons. Firstly, many people now have desk jobs and travel everywhere by car, so they burn far fewer calories than previous generations. Secondly, cheap processed food full of sugar and fat is available on every corner. As a result, *obesity* has become a serious problem, and it often leads to *chronic* conditions such as diabetes and heart disease.

p3.q: Should healthcare be free for everyone?
p3.a: In principle, I think basic *healthcare* should be free, because nobody should be denied *treatment* simply because they are poor. However, completely free systems are very expensive and can lead to long waiting lists. A sensible compromise might be free care for essential services, with small fees for non-urgent procedures, so that governments can fund the system sustainably.

writing.q: In many countries, the number of people who are overweight is increasing rapidly. What are the main causes of this problem? What measures could be taken to solve it? Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
essay: Over recent decades, *obesity* rates have risen dramatically in both wealthy and developing nations, placing enormous pressure on public *healthcare* systems. This essay will argue that the problem stems mainly from modern diets and *sedentary* lifestyles, and that it requires action from governments, schools and individuals alike.

The most significant cause is the widespread availability of cheap, high-calorie food. Fast-food outlets and supermarkets promote sugary snacks and drinks aggressively, and busy families often choose convenience over nutrition. At the same time, physical activity has declined sharply. Many adults spend eight hours a day sitting at a desk, while children increasingly prefer video games to outdoor play. Consequently, people consume far more energy than they burn, and this imbalance gradually leads to weight gain and *chronic* illnesses such as type 2 diabetes.

Several measures could reverse this trend. Firstly, governments could tax sugary drinks and require clear nutritional labels, as the United Kingdom has done with its levy on soft drinks. Secondly, schools should provide healthy meals and daily sports lessons, so that good habits are formed early. Finally, doctors could focus more on *prevention*, offering regular check-ups and advice before weight-related problems become serious. Such steps would not only improve individual *well-being* but also raise *life expectancy* and reduce long-term medical costs.

In conclusion, rising *obesity* is largely the result of unhealthy diets and inactive lifestyles. While personal responsibility certainly matters, especially when it comes to daily food choices, coordinated action by governments, schools and health professionals is essential to tackle this growing problem.
